run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-15T11:29:43Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert for otel-demo/frontend-proxy is explained by two verified error sources in frontend-proxy's own spans. (1) A window-wide source present from the first observable sample: frontend-proxy ingress 504 'UT response_timeout' on POST /api/checkout. One complete trace shows the proxy aborting after 15.0 s while the frontend POST /api/checkout span ran 89.1 s because checkout's internal 'orders publish' span blocked 88.9 s and failed with otel.status_description 'circuit breaker is open'; every other checkout downstream call in that trace was fast and returned gRPC 0. checkout pod logs independently show 'Failed to write message: circuit breaker is open', 'kafka server: Request was for a topic or partition that does not exist on this broker' and metadata requests to kafka:9092 timing out, while both kafka pods log repeating KRaft '[QuorumController id=1] assignReplicasToDirs: event failed with StaleBrokerEpochException ... Expected broker epoch 17, but got broker epoch 10'. The checkout 504 production is observable from 11:33:06 (access logs) and 11:30:43 (metrics) through 11:57:55, so it alone holds frontend-proxy's error rate above 0. (2) A time-bounded second source: the ad container in pod ad-554b849958-4chjq was OOMKilled at 11:47:24Z after its working set reached the 450Mi limit; with a single ad replica no ad server spans appear for the windows ending 11:52:43-11:56:43, frontend error spans on grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds, tcp.connect and GET /api/data ran 11:48:43-11:56:43, frontend-proxy egress errors peaked 0.77 spans/s at 11:52:43 and ingress errors peaked 1.24 spans/s at 11:54:43, with frontend-proxy access logs showing GET /api/data -> 500 in that period. The alert's own 'current: 1.5999' at 11:29:43 could not be reconciled: Prometheus returns samples only from 11:30:43 and no RequestErrorRate rule is loaded, so what drove the initial firing before 11:30 remains unknown.

Exception message: Expected broker epoch 17, but got broker epoch 10" plus matching "[ControllerApis nodeId=1] Unexpected error handling request ... Deployment ad has spec.replicas=1 and container ad limits cpu 50m / memory 450Mi with requests cpu 10m / memory 225Mi. Frontend (service_name="frontend") ERROR spans in 11:48:43-11:56:43 were confined to span_name "GET /api/data", "executing api route (pages) /api/data" and "grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds" (together peaking at 0.7667 spans/s at 11:54:43) plus "tcp.connect" (0.0259-0.0407 spans/s); they were 0 at 11:30:43-11:46:43 and 0 at 12:00:43 and 12:02:43, while frontend "POST /api/checkout", "POST", "GET /api/cart", "POST /api/cart", grpc.oteldemo.CartService/GetCart, AddItem and CheckoutService/PlaceOrder had 0 ERROR rate throughout.

Among the 22 otel-demo pods, only ad-554b849958-4chjq had a nonzero restart count (1); frontend-675fd7b5c5-djtdf, frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-59tsm, checkout-5dccddf8bb-vn95l and the kafka pods all showed restartCount 0 and ready containers, so no pod crash other than ad was observed.

Other services' ERROR-span rates did not move with the frontend-proxy error rate: accounting "orders receive", payment (GET, dns.lookup, tcp.connect), frontend cart/checkout client calls, and shipping/currency/email/quote/product-catalog operations returned 0 across the queried points; only small flagd EventStream errors (0.0037 spans/s) on ad, fraud-detection and recommendation appear plus ad's post-restart flagd errors, so the frontend-proxy error rate is not explained by broad multi-service failure.

Primary driver of frontend-proxy's nonzero error rate: the chronic POST /api/checkout 504 upstream timeouts rooted in checkout's Kafka publish path. The proxy aborts at its 15 s timeout while checkout's "orders publish" span blocks about 89 s and fails with "circuit breaker is open"; checkout logs show the producer unable to reach broker kafka:9092 (metadata i/o timeout, broker deregistered, 'topic or partition does not exist on this broker'). This error production exists from the first observable data (11:30:43 metrics, 11:33:06 access log) through 11:57:55, so it explains an error rate above 0 independently of the ad restart.

Second, time-bounded contributor: the ad container OOMKill at 11:47:24Z removed the only ad replica from service (no ad server spans for the 5-minute windows ending 11:52:43, 11:54:43 and 11:56:43), which produced the frontend's grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds and tcp.connect error spans and GET /api/data 500 responses in 11:48:43-11:56:43 and therefore the frontend-proxy egress ERROR spans (peak 0.77 spans/s at 11:52:43) and part of the ingress ERROR rise to 1.24 spans/s at 11:54:43.

Deepest observed cause of the checkout publish failures is the Kafka KRaft broker-epoch mismatch: both brokers log StaleBrokerEpochException with "Expected broker epoch 17, but got broker epoch 10" for brokerId=1 and repeated "50 assignments failed; global error: Response-level error: STALE_BROKER_EPOCH", consistent with the producer's 'topic or partition does not exist on this broker' errors; why the epoch diverged (controller-side reset, broker restart/identity change, or storage/state issue) is not established by the available evidence.

Increase the ad container's memory headroom (its 450Mi limit was reached exactly at the OOMKill; raise the limit and tune the heap/request) and consider running more than one ad replica so single-pod loss does not take the whole ad service out of service.

Investigate the Kafka quorum/broker state behind the StaleBrokerEpochException (expected epoch 17 vs broker epoch 10) and the missing 'orders' topic metadata on broker 1, and review the checkout Kafka producer settings plus the frontend-proxy/router 15 s upstream timeout, since an approximately 89 s blocked publish can never complete inside that timeout.

gaps: The alert's own value (current: 1.5999 at 2026-11-15T11:29:43Z) cannot be reconciled with the available series: every traces_span_metrics_calls_total query returned samples only from 11:30:43 onward (source_start_at 11:30:43), so the first observable frontend-proxy ingress ERROR rate is 0.18 spans/s and egress is 0; what produced 1.6 at firing time is unknown.
No alerting rule named RequestErrorRate is loaded in the queried Prometheus (list_prometheus_rules returned no_data), so the alert's exact expression, metric and window could not be verified.

The previous ad container's logs are unavailable (fetch_pod_logs for ad-554b849958-4chjq returned no_data with 'previous terminated container ad not found'), so pre-OOM behaviour is known only from cAdvisor metrics and the OOMKilled last state.

The frontend pod frontend-675fd7b5c5-djtdf returned no log lines for 11:45-12:00 (no_data, 0 bytes read), so frontend application-side error text could not be read; frontend impact rests on its own error spans and the frontend-proxy access logs.

Kafka log reads were cut by the 4 MiB read limit and newest-line limits; the origin of the broker epoch mismatch (why the controller expects epoch 17 while broker 1 presents epoch 10, and whether either kafka pod was previously restarted or its identity reset) is not determinable, and the change_history integration is not integrated so no change record is available.
Ad's flagd ResolveBoolean ERROR spans right after its restart (0.1417 spans/s at 11:58:43, 0.128 spans/s at 12:00:43) are observed but not explained by the collected evidence.
Time before 11:30:43 is not observable in the metric series, so it is unknown whether the checkout 504 production started earlier, worsened, or was the sole cause at the alert's 11:29:43 firing time.

A traces_search for frontend-proxy spans in 11:40-12:00 returned RESULT_TOO_LARGE and its rows were not read, so the broader span population in that window remains unexamined beyond the targeted queries.
next_steps: Inspect kafka quorum-controller/controller logs and metadata for the divergence between expected broker epoch 17 and broker epoch 10, and whether the 'orders' topic partitions exist on broker 1.

Review change history for the otel-demo stack around 11:17-11:30 (all pods start 11:17:44-11:19:36) to see whether the Kafka state and the ad memory pressure predate the alert; the change_history integration is not available in this Run.
Check the checkout Kafka producer settings (circuit breaker and metadata timeouts) and the frontend-proxy/router 15 s upstream timeout, which converts an 89 s blocked checkout into a 504.
Raise or right-size the ad container memory limit (450Mi was hit exactly) and evaluate running more than one ad replica.
Confirm the RequestErrorRate alert rule expression in the alerting stack, since it is not present in the queried Prometheus rules.
